As a woman farmer with no schooling in North East Nigeria, I have learned to farm by watching my mother and by my own experience over many seasons. I do not have money to buy chemical fertilizer for this bean plot, and beans can fix their own nitrogen from the air anyway, but I will spread manure from our goats and chickens to keep the soil strong. I will plant seeds I saved from last year’s harvest because improved seeds are expensive and difficult to get without traveling to the big market, but I will buy some pesticide to protect the pods from insects that always attack cowpea here. The rains should be enough, so I will not irrigate. My children and I will do most of the planting, weeding, and harvesting, but I will hire a few young people from the village to help during the busiest weeks because we also have other plots to tend.
